messages:
Alex: Ran an nsys capture on the 8-GPU replica after the batcher heuristics change. Seeing repeated H2D memcpy blocks that serialize kernels for ~2.2-2.6ms spikes. Waterfall attached in my next post :eyes:
Maria: Did you capture the CPU scheduling slices? Could be the host copy thread getting preempted. Which host thread is issuing the memcpy?
Alex: It's the copy thread in the 'prefetch' worker using the pinned pool. nvtx shows `prefetch:start` -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> `prefetch:done`. But the memcpy appears as a long host-side stall in the nsight timeline. Command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=memcpy_wakeup_report --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --stats=true --quiet -- ./run_serving_workload.sh
```
Sam: If the host thread is getting preempted you will see a gap between enqueue time and the memcpy actually showing on the device. Look for `sched_wakeup` / `sched_switch` events in the trace.
Jordan: Also note: after the recent kernel selection change the small-batch path switched to the fused attention kernel. Kernel time dropped but memcpy waits increased. Could be different temp-buffer behavior causing more/bigger host copies.
Maria: Can you export a perfetto view? In some captures I've seen `sched_wakeup` exactly 1.7-1.9ms before the copy shows up on the GPU timeline. That aligns with host wake latency.
Alex: Perfetto slice: `pid=batcher (thread prefetch) sched_wakeup -> sleep -> memcpy enqueue` at 09:12:17.345. NVidia timeline shows stream 3 memcpy then stream 0 kernel waits. Snippet of the trace filter I used:
```
# perfetto query: show slices where name contains memcpy or sched_wakeup
select ts, name, pid from slice where name like '%memcpy%' or name='sched_wakeup'
```
infra-bot: deploy-batcher v2 rolled out to 6/8 hosts at 09:12 UTC :rocket:
Sam: Quick repro idea: run a single-GPU job with `--batcher=heuristic_v2 --kv-prefetch=on` and inspect nvtx markers. I saw two back-to-back memcpy ops; the second seems to force a host sync in our traces.
Maria: :thinking: Two things to try: 1) flip `kv_prefetch_async=true` so prefetch uses a dedicated non-blocking copy stream, 2) raise copy thread priority (SCHED_FIFO) to reduce preemption windows.
Alex: I'll try the priority change + pinning the prefetch thread to a CPU core and re-run the nsys capture tonight. If host wake latency goes down we have a short-term mitigation.
Jordan: Also file a follow-up: capture kernel launch attributes (shared mem, temp alloc) for the fused vs old kernels and run a microbench. If temp alloc size increased, the driver might be serializing DMA to manage memory pressure.
Maria: If reproducible, consider moving prefetch earlier (when request first queued) to smooth out H2D peaks instead of doing all prefetches just-in-time. That could reduce the head-of-line blocking.
Alex: Thanks — I'll attach the nsight snapshots and the perfetto export in the thread once I have the next capture. Ping @Sam if you want to pair on the microbench tomorrow. :+1:
